default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1218.title: Dollar lead on the index
E-1218.hypothesis: WIN and the dollar are negatively linked and WDO often reprices first; when the dollar moves sharply and the index has not yet moved, the index catches up in the opposite direction.

E-1219.title: Day-open retest bounce
E-1219.hypothesis: After the day has drifted well away from its open, a return to the opening price that closes back on the trend side shows the day's early buyers/sellers still defend it; follow the original direction.

E-1220.title: Up-bar share extreme fade
E-1220.hypothesis: When nearly every recent bar closes the same way the move is crowded and the next marginal buyer/seller is exhausted; fade the first bar the share reaches the extreme.

E-1221.title: Gap-bar fill
E-1221.hypothesis: A bar that opens with a gap from the previous close that is large for the recent range and then closes back through the previous close shows the gap was an overreaction; follow the fill.

E-1222.title: Sloped-VWAP pullback
E-1222.hypothesis: When the session VWAP itself is rising or falling faster than usual, the day's average cost is trending; a dip to VWAP that closes back on the trend side is where trend traders add.

E-1223.title: Rolling z-score stretch fade
E-1223.hypothesis: A close several standard deviations from its own rolling mean is a liquidity-driven stretch that mean-reverts within minutes; fade the first bar to get there.

E-1224.title: Midday box break follow
E-1224.hypothesis: The thin midday hour builds a box of resting orders; the first close outside it after the box ends signals the return of the afternoon's directional flow (US open); follow it.

E-1226.title: Volume-surge range break
E-1226.hypothesis: A close beyond the recent range on volume well above the usual for that minute of day means real participation, not a thin poke; follow it.

E-1227.title: Absorption after a wide bar
E-1227.hypothesis: A wide bar followed by a smaller bar that closes at its far extreme and back over the wide bar's open means the push was absorbed by the other side; trade the reversal.
